title: Industrial subdivision beside Huron Natural Area
subtitle: Also: Woodhaven Road rezoning referred, Reinhardt and Windom demolitions, engagement policy update, and backyard and fourplex housing check-in.
overview: The committee spent most of the evening on a draft plan of subdivision for 1700 Strasburg Road and McBrine Drive, next to the Huron Natural Area. It recommended draft approval {{vote:m5}}, after dozens of delegates, many of them residents, students and nature advocates, spoke against it. The land is privately owned and already zoned for industrial use, so the decision shaped how it is divided and protected, not whether it can be developed. Staff said the plan would add a wetland, a wildlife corridor and trail connections, and could support up to 1800 jobs.

The committee also recommended that a rezoning for 137 Woodhaven Road be referred to the November 10 Council meeting. That gives time to explore support for tenants who could be displaced {{vote:m4}}. It recommended approving demolitions on Reinhardt Street and Windom Road {{vote:m1}} {{vote:m2}}, and directed staff to update the Community Engagement Policy {{vote:m3}}.

On the Enabling 4 Units one-year check-in, the committee recommended that Council endorse staff's next steps {{vote:m6}}. Councillors raised concerns about privacy and the size of some backyard units.
These are recommendations. Council will consider them at a later meeting.

decisions.item: Strasburg Road draft plan of subdivision
decisions.detail: The committee recommended draft approval of a 10-lot industrial subdivision at 1700 Strasburg Road and McBrine Drive with staff's conditions, an industrial subdivision agreement and endorsement of the urban design brief {{vote:m5}}.

The committee recommended referring the rezoning application to the November 10, 2025 Council meeting so the Ward Councillor, consultant and staff can discuss and explore support for residents who could be displaced.
The committee recommended that Council endorse the staff next steps from the one-year review of the policy allowing up to four units on residential lots.
The committee directed staff to update the Community Engagement Policy and bring it forward through a future Corporate Policy review update report.
The committee recommended approving demolition of a single detached dwelling at 15 Reinhardt Street and a duplex at 16 Reinhardt Street.
The committee recommended approving demolition of the dwellings at 32 and 42 Windom Road.

debate: Delegates opposing the Strasburg Road subdivision raised loss of natural area, habitat fragmentation, turtle nesting, coyote and wildlife impacts, noise, traffic and the scale of development. They asked why more industrial land is needed given reported vacancies elsewhere.

A delegate who reviewed the environmental impact study pointed to what they saw as inconsistencies and asked for a deferral. The consultant and staff said the study's findings were sound. Staff said they would re-check the points raised and that detailed design and further consultation would follow draft approval.

Staff and supporting councillors stressed that the land is privately owned, already zoned industrial and was sold by the City as surplus. They said the owner could build one large user without a subdivision. The plan secures a wetland, a wildlife corridor and buffers, and about one-third of the site would go to the City.

On Woodhaven Road, delegates cited noise, privacy, parking, emergency access and neighbourhood character. Current tenants said they feared displacement and had not been notified directly. Several councillors said they were comfortable with the density but wanted firmer commitments to tenants, including rent after return.

On backyard units, some councillors raised privacy, size and lack of neighbour notice, while others supported the approach as gentle intensification. Staff said parking rules should not change for now and complaints remain few.
